html:
The Orapa diamond mine in central Botswana is the largest diamond mine in the world by area. It was found by De Beers geologists in 1967, a year after Botswana's independence, and began production in 1971.

At independence Botswana was one of the poorest countries on earth, with a few kilometres of paved road. The diamonds of Orapa, and of the even richer Jwaneng mine opened in 1982, changed that.

The government of Seretse Khama made a deal in which it and De Beers became equal partners in a joint company, Debswana. The state used its share to build roads, schools and clinics and saved much of the rest.

Botswana became one of the fastest-growing economies in the world for decades and a middle-income country, a rare case in Africa of minerals bringing wealth without war or plunder, unlike the "blood diamonds" of Sierra Leone and Angola. It still depends heavily on diamonds, which makes it vulnerable when prices fall.
